title: Integration discovery - Atlantic Payments
summary: Initial integration discovery focusing on SDK support (LangChain / LlamaIndex), gateway/proxy architecture, rate limits/quotas, and observability hooks. Customer is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private due to data residency and latency needs. Agreed next steps: send pricing + security pack, share LangChain examples, schedule Dedicated demo with perf tests, and define PoC scope.
topics: SDKs and integration (official SDKs, REST vs gRPC)
LangChain and LlamaIndex connectors and examples
Gateway/proxy and network flow (VPC, peering, egress)
Rate limits, quotas, lots and bursting
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs and security requirements
action_items: Sofia Ramos - send Dedicated sizing worksheet, pricing tiers, and draft SLA - due 2027-06-12
Marcus Lee - share LangChain integration example repo and LlamaIndex notebook (simple retriever flow) - due 2027-06-11
Karen Wu - provide expected throughput profile (queries/sec) and 95th pct latency SLO - due 2027-06-14
Liam O'Connor - confirm VPC peering IP ranges and firewall egress rules - due 2027-06-12
next_steps: Redwood to send pricing and security pack (SOC2 report, whitepaper, KMS options)
Schedule technical demo of Dedicated runtime with live perf tests (Marcus to run)
Agree on PoC scope and success metrics (throughput, latency, cost per token)
meeting_header:
Date: 2027-06-09
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Ramos (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Karen Wu (Atlantic CTO), Dev Patel (Engineering Manager), Liam O'Connor (DevOps)
Recording ID: ff-20270609-ATL-001
transcript:
00:00 Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Sofia from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. Marcus our SE is with me, he'll walk through the technical bits. Uh, Karen, you said you and team are evaluating Hosted, Dedicated and Private?
00:28 Karen: Yeah, hi. Thanks. We want to understand integration surface area — SDK support, LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors, and how the gateway would sit in our infra. Also need clarity on rate limits and observability.
00:55 Marcus: Great. Quick agenda: SDKs and examples, LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters, network/gateway patterns (VPC, proxy, peering), quotas and bursting, observability hooks, and then Q&A. Sound good?
01:12 Dev: Sounds good. One quick constraint — we have sub-100ms P95 for some paths, and a lot of traffic comes from EU.
01:30 Sofia: Noted. On latency we can talk about Dedicated or Private; Hosted can be fine if you accept some routing variance.
01:45 Marcus: On SDKs: we have official SDKs for Node/Python/Go, plus a simple REST and gRPC gateway. The SDKs handle streaming and function-calling. There's also example integrations for LangChain and LlamaIndex — small repos we can share.
02:10 Dev: Are those examples recent? We use LangChain v0.1x and LlamaIndex — plugin compatibility has been a pain with other providers.
02:32 Marcus: They were updated in May — should be compatible with the v0.1x series but there are some naming inconsistencies in the transcribed code comments (we saw that in other customer's runs). We'll send a notebook showing a retriever + generative chain with LlamaIndex.
02:50 Karen: For data residency we need EU-only processing. Does Redwood Hosted support region pinning?
03:05 Sofia: Yes, we have region controls; Hosted has EU regions. For strict residency and networking, Dedicated or Private are better since they give control of capacity and VPC options.
03:25 Liam: If we do Dedicated, what's the network setup? Can we put a Gateway in our VPC?
03:40 Marcus: You can either forward requests through our managed gateway or run a customer-facing gateway/proxy in your VPC that talks to the Redwood control plane. For Private deployments we support a full on-prem package. For Dedicated we typically offer VPC peering or private link depending on cloud.
04:05 Karen: Any gotchas on latency with proxying?
04:18 Marcus: There's an extra network hop; typical added latency is 5-20ms depending on peering. But the big latency wins come from model placement and kernel optimizations. For strict 50ms P95 you may need Dedicated + model pinning.
04:40 Dev: How about KV cache? We saw mention of prefix caching and KV cache in docs — is that exposed to customers?
04:55 Marcus: We expose cache controls at the route level; there's automatic prefix caching and optional explicit KV cache APIs. Note: transcriptions sometimes render it as "K V cash" in our notes, haha.
05:10 Karen: Rate limits — we have bursty traffic. Can you do bursting above committed capacity?
05:25 Sofia: Yes, with Dedicated you get reserved capacity and a burst pool for spikes; Hosted has quotas and bursting but it's more governed by tier. We can configure soft and hard rate limits per API key and route.
05:45 Dev: Are quotas enforced at token level or request level? We bill per token but limit both, right?
06:00 Marcus: Exactly. Token-based billing, but rate limiting is often requests/sec or concurrent tokens; we provide per-route metrics so you can enforce both.
06:18 Karen: Observability — we need tracing, sampling, per-route cost breakdowns and logs for audits.
06:32 Marcus: Our Console gives token-level cost breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and a tracing hook you can push to Jaeger/Datadog. We also emit audit logs and integrate with KMS for encryption keys.
06:50 Liam: Do you provide telemetry hooks (OpenTelemetry)?
07:00 Marcus: We have an OpenTelemetry exporter and a small client lib that emits spans for each request. It also annotates model, route, and token counts.
07:18 Dev: If we proxy through our gateway does Redwood still get those spans?
07:30 Marcus: Yes, either the proxy forwards tracing headers or you can push aggregated telemetry from the gateway. We can share an example proxy config.
07:45 Karen: Security — SOC2, SSO, KMS, and logs are must-haves. Also need to know about data retention and purge policies.
08:00 Sofia: We can share our SOC2 report and security pack. We support SAML/SSO (Okta, Azure AD), RBAC, and customer-managed KMS for Private. Hosted has managed KMS with envelope encryption and an option for bring-your-own-key with enterprise plans.
08:25 Dev: For Private on-prem, what's the deployment footprint? GPU requirements?
08:38 Marcus: For on-prem we provide a package that runs in your cluster; depends on model class — gpt-like 70B vs 13B have different footprints. We'll include a sizing worksheet. For Dedicated we size GPU pools and suggest autoscaling policies.
09:00 Karen: Can the SDKs operate over internal network only? We want to avoid public egress for some workloads.
09:15 Marcus: Yes, with VPC peering or private link the calls can stay internal. For Private you can run entirely air-gapped.
09:28 Dev: Are there any existing customers in payments/finance you can reference?
09:35 Sofia: We have a few references in fintech; I'll include a short reference list in the pack.
09:50 Karen: On integration: how opinionated are the SDKs? We prefer minimal wrapper so we can instrument.
10:05 Marcus: SDKs are lightweight; they provide helpers for streaming and function-calls but you can use raw REST/gRPC if you want full control.
10:18 Dev: LangChain — any example of tool-calling or function-calling patterns?
10:30 Marcus: Yes, we have an example where a LangChain agent calls external tools and the Redwood SDK handles the function call schema. We'll share that repo.
10:45 [crosstalk] Liam: And LlamaIndex — retrieval speed for large corpora?
10:55 Marcus: Retrieval speed depends on vector DB and embedding latency. We support server-side embeddings and you can store vectors in your DB. We also have recommendations to colocate embeddings service near the model to reduce roundtrip.
11:20 Karen: What about rate-limiting for embeddings-heavy workloads?
11:30 Marcus: We recommend a separate quota for embeddings routes. You can have different rate limits and different instance types for embeddings to isolate cost.
11:45 Dev: Billing transparency — need per-route token breakdown for internal chargeback.
11:55 Marcus: Console exposes token counts and cost per route; we can also push CSV exports for billing.
12:10 Karen: Ok. Let's talk PoC — we want a 2-week PoC to validate latency and cost on our EU traffic. Can Redwood run perf tests?
12:22 Sofia: Yes. Typical PoC: agree on dataset and traffic profile, Redwood runs perf tests on Dedicated or Hosted EU region, and we measure throughput/latency/cost. Marcus can run a dedicated test harness.
12:40 Marcus: For the perf run we'll want a representative prompt set and concurrency profile, plus whether you'll use caching. If you provide the sample traffic we can simulate and show expected units and latency.
13:05 Karen: About caching — prefix caching, does it change semantics? We need determinism for some flows.
13:18 Marcus: Prefix caching is opt-in per route; it short-circuits repeated prefixes to save tokens but you can disable it. For deterministic flows you can turn off heuristics.
13:35 Dev: Any notes on quantization or model variants? We sometimes need cheaper variants for background tasks.
13:48 Marcus: We recommend quantized variants for throughput-heavy non-critical tasks. We can serve multiple model variants and route rules let you pick by workload.
14:05 Karen: How fast are rollouts and fallback policies? If a model upgrade causes regressions we need immediate fallback.
14:18 Marcus: We support canary rollouts, A/B, and automatic fallback to a pinned model version when quality regressions are detected. The Console has rollout controls.
14:35 Dev: Observability again — can we get token-level traces tied to request IDs?
14:45 Marcus: Yes, we emit request IDs and token counts per span; you can correlate in your tracing.
15:00 Sofia: Quick check — any blockers for proceeding to PoC?
15:08 Karen: Need cost estimate, security docs, and LangChain examples to validate our stack. Also approval from procurement.
15:20 Sofia: We'll send the pricing and security pack. Marcus will share examples and a notebook. We'll put together a PoC plan for two weeks.
15:35 Liam: One small things — firewall requires exact IP ranges.
15:42 Marcus: We'll include IP ranges and peering instructions in the network doc.
16:00 [later in call, deeper technical follow-ups led by Marcus]
16:05 Marcus: Example of gateway config: NGINX or Envoy in front of the SDK, forward original trace headers, mTLS to Redwood endpoint. If you prefer we can provide a sample envoy config.
16:30 Dev: What's the concurrency model in the SDK? Does it multiplex connections?
16:45 Marcus: SDK uses connection pooling; we also allow persistent streams for lower latency. For high concurrency we recommend batching at the client side or using our continuous batching features.
17:10 Karen: Is there an SLA for token latency or availability?
17:22 Sofia: For Dedicated we provide SLA-backed uptime and latency targets in enterprise contracts. Hosted has tiered SLAs.
17:40 Dev: About quotas — can we change them dynamically?
17:52 Marcus: Yes, quotas are configurable via Console and API. We also provide programmatic quota change requests for spikes.
18:10 Karen: Anything else?
18:18 Sofia: Recap: Redwood to send security pack + SOC2, pricing and Dedicated sizing worksheet; Marcus to share LangChain/LlamaIndex examples and envoy/nginx proxy configs; customer to share traffic profile and firewall rules. We'll schedule Dedicated demo and perf run.
18:40 Karen: Great. Thanks everyone.
18:45 Sofia: Thanks — we'll follow up by end of week with the pack.
18:50 [meeting ends, recording stops]
